purpose: decide whether semantic journal + separate recovery materially improves current Rinne under equal guarantees; not to prove a new protocol

variants.description: strong path carries the same protected event plus the full recovery checkpoint at each canon boundary
strong path carries protected event/delta; provisional recovery checkpoints run asynchronously at the declared RPO; protected semantic snapshots compact the journal separately
known event-sourcing + the same quorum/consensus service, exact same semantic event encoding, compaction and recovery RPO as semantic-journal
variants.expected: should match semantic-journal strong-path cost absent an implementation-quality difference

fairnessRequirements: same Rinne build and gameplay workload
same crash-fault durability target and authority mechanism
same provisional recovery RPO and recovery test
same safety hard gates; any safety violation fails regardless of speed
no pooled endpoint statistic may hide the slowest required device under the existing performance-contract rules
startCohort: 2-3 physical peers on fixed Wi-Fi, then broader network profiles and 30-device certification separately
acceptance: all safety keys are zero/within their existing hard semantics
semantic-journal may beat all-state-strong on strong-path bytes/latency when replaceable/recovery material is actually removed from synchronous commit
semantic-journal is not called a protocol win if fair-known-event-sourcing matches it
a provisional RPO setting is accepted only after user-visible rollback/recovery quality and bandwidth/latency are measured together
no absolute threshold is invented for metrics currently marked calibration-required
